digest.component_or_area: completion verifier context assembly and file prefetching
propositions: Completion verifier receives only fenced ticket_context with zero file contents, requiring 84-158 agentic read_file/search_files requests per run dominated by round-trip latency, with 67-82% of distinct reads already declared in file_impact but fetched again.

Four captured close-gate (graph=False) traces show runaway loops driven by agent re-discovery of file_impact contents; close gate verifies own completion only (not descendants), so close-path prefetch must honor that boundary—only own file_impact, no subtree walk.

Prefetch mechanism appends bounded, ranked file_impact contents plus referencing-commit diffs to the byte-stable fenced ticket_context, with per-file and 30k-token aggregate caps; oversize files skeleton-compressed before drop; rides the existing automatic message-tail cache and physical_context_ceiling validation.

Recovery batched successors inherit the assembled ticket_context (carrying prefetch once, not per-criterion) via static cache_prefix; prefetch bytes included in ceiling validation so oversize prefetch trims rather than raises.

Trusted anti-anchoring guidance (confirm full bodies against working tree, re-read skeleton-marked files) lives in completion_verifier.md static prefix before volatile marker, so successor_system_prompt inherits it from single source.

Live A/B on real closed tickets (f6fc 25→11 requests = 56%, e6a0 20→14 = 30%, both PASS=PASS) clears 20% reduction target; close-path own-file_impact coverage 29-33% of baseline reads; graph=True subtree-union coverage pinned by unit oracle synthetic fixture.
